page.summary: Spend a toolbox on the generator that needs progress now, then decide whether another recharge is worth leaving the job.

verdict.recommendation: Choose this when you can turn limited toolbox charges into meaningful generator progress, not merely faster work on the safest generator.
verdict.soloQ: Pick a reachable important generator and watch for uncovered rescues before leaving to recharge.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Agree which generator gets the burst and who covers repair or rescue while you recharge.
verdict.mainWeakness: Your item and recharge time are finite investments; losing the toolbox or repeatedly leaving objectives undermines the plan.

plans.label: Toolbox recharge tool
plans.why: A single recharge tool for a toolbox-focused plan. The other slots depend on your wider build; this is not a fixed four-perk recipe.

choices.whyItsHere: Make another toolbox repair window possible when the return is worth the locker detour. Recharge is a choice about tempo, not a job you must repeat whenever the item empties.

item.name: Toolbox
item.why: The strategy spends toolbox charges to concentrate repair progress. Bring a toolbox for a reliable opening; without a usable one, continue ordinary repairs instead of playing as though the burst is still available.

opening: Identify a generator whose completion would loosen the Killer's control of the remaining objectives. Check that you can work on it now before spending your item.

rows.situation: You have charges and a useful repair window on an important generator.
rows.action: Use the toolbox on that target rather than automatically emptying it into the first safe generator you touch. If the Killer closes the window, leave before a short burst costs a down.
rows.why: The point is to buy progress where it changes the next rotation, not to maximize time holding the item button.

rows.situation: The toolbox is depleted and Built to Last still has a recharge available.
rows.action: Check for urgent rescues and whether staying on the generator could finish it. Take a safe locker detour with the depleted toolbox only when the next repair window can repay the interruption.
rows.why: Leaving useful work to recharge can lose more tempo than the recovered charges return.

rows.situation: You have already used the recharge tool and are considering another trip.
rows.action: Judge the remaining value again instead of repeating the opening routine. If travel or danger makes the return poor, keep repairing without the toolbox.
rows.why: Later recharges give less item value; the same detour becomes harder to justify as the Trial changes.

rows.situation: Your toolbox is lost, unavailable or cannot be safely recovered.
rows.action: Switch to ordinary repairs or the needed rescue. Do not chase the item into pressure just to keep the build's original plan alive.
rows.why: The team still needs progress even when your specialized resource is gone.

abortWhen: Skip the locker when a hook needs immediate attention, the Killer is pressuring the route or the current generator is better finished now.
Stop planning further item bursts when the toolbox or recharge opportunity is gone; use normal repair and rescue decisions.

soloQ: Do not assume someone else will cover the hook during your recharge; check teammate activity before leaving.
coordinatedSwf: Call your intended generator and recharge detour. Another player can keep the agreed objective moving or take the rescue without duplicating your travel.

weaknesses: Charges run out, later recharges return less, and a locker detour spends time that could have gone into repair.
killerCounterplay: Item denial or pressure that drives you off the intended generator can remove the repair window you saved charges for.
commonMistakes: Spending all charges on an easy generator while the dangerous cluster remains untouched.
Making a recharge trip while still holding a partly used item instead of checking the depleted-item condition.
Treating every possible recharge as mandatory, even when a rescue or ordinary repair would matter more.
